scope.summary: This standard specifies the material quality, general dimensions, tolerances, and proof test loads for ship's snatch blocks used with wire ropes corresponding to various safe working loads (SWL). Snatch blocks are defined as blocks designed with a hinged strap to enable the insertion of a wire rope onto the sheave at any position along the length of the rope.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification / Mechanical Dimensions (Marine Outfitting / Cargo Gear)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Quality and Performance Specification. Since snatch blocks are marine outfitting cargo-handling components rather than consumer products, they are certified on a voluntary basis under the BIS ISI Certification scheme. However, compliance with IS 6140:1971 is universally required by marine surveyors, classification societies (such as IRS, LRS, or DNV-GL), the Indian Navy, and dock safety inspectors under Indian Dock Labour Regulations to approve shipboard cargo gear and rigging systems.

requirements.detail: Every snatch block satisfying this standard may be legibly marked with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) as a guarantee of quality and load-bearing safety.

Snatch blocks using wire ropes are strictly restricted to the following onboard operations: a) Deck lead blocks; b) Span blocks single or double reeved for topping an unloaded derrick; c) Lead blocks for guy tackle runners, provided the runner is turned to an angle of not more than 90°.
Specifies five standard block nominal sizes corresponding to safe working loads (SWL) and sheave sizes: Size 1 (150 mm cheek), Size 2 (200 mm), Size 3 (240 mm), Size 5 (320 mm), and Size 8 (400 mm).
The snatch block as a whole must be subjected to a static proof load test. The test load must be exactly four (4) times the declared Safe Working Load (SWL) of the block.
The proof test load must be applied and held continuously for a minimum period of five (5) minutes.

At the conclusion of the proof test, the snatch block must be disassembled, and all components must be carefully inspected for permanent deformation, cracks, or other structural defects. Blocks shall be approved subject to showing zero permanent deformation.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS : 6140 - 1971 (Reaffirmed 2022) is the national Indian Standard specification governing snatch blocks (hinged-strap wire rope pulleys) utilized for shipboard rigging and cargo gear outfitting. Developed under the technical supervision of the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee (MCPD 1) with considerable design assistance from the German standard DIN 82220, this standard unifies the dimensions, materials, and testing parameters for blocks across five nominal sizes (ranging from 150 mm to 400 mm). To guarantee absolute maritime safety and prevent failure during load handling, it enforces strict operational constraints—limiting wire-rope snatch blocks to deck leads, topping spans, and limited-angle guy tackle runners—and mandates that the assembled block withstand a proof load of four times its Safe Working Load (SWL) for five minutes without exhibiting any permanent deformation or structural cracks upon disassembly.
